Three versions are ready. Each one is the same library with the same two saved links — the *only* difference is how you add a tag. Please try them in order and notice which feels most natural.

**Version A — type & enter** → **http://maker:4001/tags-a.html**
On the MDN card, click **"+ add tag"**, type `reading`, and press Enter. A tag chip appears. Add one or two more the same way, and remove one with its little ×. This is fast, free-form typing.

**Version B — pick from your tags** → **http://maker:4001/tags-b.html**
On the MDN card, click **"+ add tag"**. A little panel pops up showing tags you've already used (plus a few examples). Click `reading` to add it, click an on-tag to remove it, or type a brand-new tag at the bottom and press Enter. This keeps your tags consistent and avoids near-duplicates.

**Version C — details panel** → **http://maker:4001/tags-c.html**
Click anywhere on the MDN card (not the title link) — a panel slides in from the right showing that link's details. Type a tag in the field and press Enter; remove one with its ×. This gives each link a dedicated space where tags (and later, notes) live together.

A couple of things I decided that I'd like your read on:
- In all three, I **lowercase tags automatically** and **prevent exact duplicates on the same link** — does that matching feel right, or too aggressive?
- Tags are shown **on the card** in A and B, and **behind a click** in C.

Once you've tried all three: **which way of adding tags feels best for everyday use** — and did anything about one of them annoy you? If the perfect version is a mix (say, B's reuse of existing tags but shown inline like A), tell me that too.
